title: VPC Cost Optimizer: safemode recommendations, offline apply simulation & policy sync
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a VPC-safe cost optimization agent that generates batching and KV-caching recommendations, runs full dry-run simulations inside customer Private/VPC environments (no outbound network), and applies safe defaults with policy-driven constraints and automated rollback. The feature must operate without sending raw request data outside the customer VPC: recommendation logic runs on a packaged analysis container that consumes sampled trace files or Kafka/PS queues inside the VPC; the control plane receives only metadata (hashed model ids, aggregated stats, confidence scores) and a signed proposal. Customers can opt into automatic apply or review-only mode. Policies (customer or enterprise) must be evaluated before any live config change and enforcement must be auditable. Rollback triggers include increases in 95th percentile latency, error-rate spikes, and model-quality regressions (via provided prompt tests).
acceptance_criteria: Recommender produces batch and cache config proposals with estimated cost delta and latency delta for a 30-day request trace
Dry-run mode executes inside a customer's VPC using only local traces and produces a signed proposal artifact; no PII or full request payloads leave the VPC
Policy engine rejects proposals that violate rules (e.g., max-batch > X for single-tenant models, quantization disallowed) and logs the rejection
Automatic apply path can be toggled per-customer; when enabled, safe defaults are applied first and live metrics are monitored for 10 minutes before scaling up further
Automatic rollback reverts to pre-change config within 60s of an SLO breach (config applied via agent), and an audit entry with diff and root cause is created
Console shows per-proposal confidence, expected cost savings, and a dry-run report with before/after metric comparisons
Unit and integration tests cover offline simulator, policy evaluation, agent handshake, and rollback conditions
Feature passes security review for VPC operation and KMS/HSM key usage when signing proposals
implementation_notes: Architecture: 1) Analyzer container (customer-run) that samples traces, calculates seq-length distribution, per-model tail latency, candidate batch sizes, and KV hit curves; outputs aggregated metrics + proposal.json signed with customer KMS key. 2) Control plane component validates proposal signature, runs policy-evaluator against policy rules, and either returns approved token or rejection. 3) Private agent (already in customer fleet) pulls approved proposals and applies them via the runtime's config API with a two-step safe apply: apply conservative defaults, wait 10m, then optionally apply full proposal. Rollback implemented as atomic config diffs stored in S3-like customer bucket (or internal ledger) and an agent watchdog that monitors prometheus metrics with thresholds provided in proposal. Communications: proposals and status update go over the private control channel used by Redwood Private. Telemetry: send only aggregated delta metrics and proposal ids to control plane. Performance: offline simulation of 30 days / 1M requests should finish within 2 hours on a 4 vCPU / 16GB worker; provide a progress UI to the customer.
rollout_plan: MVP: dry-run report and signed proposals (no auto-apply) for internal beta customers
Phase 2: guarded auto-apply with safemode defaults and 10-minute observation window
Phase 3: policy sync UI and per-organization policy templates; GA with security review completed
Canary plan: enable auto-apply for <5 customers with human-on-call for first 48h
Fallback: agent has explicit revert endpoint and can be disabled via org-level toggle
test_plan: Unit tests for recommender heuristics and confidence scoring
Integration test: run analyzer container on a synthetic 1M request trace and validate proposal correctness
E2E in private staging: signed proposal roundtrip, policy rejection/accept, agent apply and rollback on injected latency spike
Security test: ensure analyzer never transmits raw token sequences; verify KMS signature verification path
Load test: analyzer completes 30-day / 5M request trace within SLAs on recommended instance size
risks: Overaggressive batch suggestions could increase tail latency for some models and customers — mitigated by safemode conservative defaults and short observation windows
Policy mismatches across orgs (customers with custom rules) may block beneficial applies — provide clear rejection reasons and suggested changes
Agent/agentless network partition might delay rollbacks — require local watchdogs to perform automatic revert when telemetry is unavailable to control plane
Simulator accuracy depends on representativeness of traces; cold-start or long-tail patterns can skew predictions
decisions: Run the heavy analysis inside the customer VPC container to avoid sending raw requests to control plane
Use KMS-signed proposals for integrity and to allow offline verification in control plane
Default auto-apply mode will be off for new customers; existing dedicated customers can opt-in via Console
Rollback window will be configurable per-org but default to 10 minutes observation and immediate revert if critical SLOs break
